name: Adjourned Planning Commission Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  ADJOURNED PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 3, 2024

An adjourned meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order by CHAIR MEDAWAR at 7:03 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Medawar, Olson, Nicklas, Repp-Loadsman, Schachter

  Commissioners Absent:  Romanelli, Yoo

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Whitney Berry, Senior Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, AUGUST 5, 2024

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 5, 2024.

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

Fred Smith, RHE Resident, asked about the names and titles of the staff members present at the
meeting. CHAIR MEDAWAR introduced staff.

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

VICE CHAIR OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240121; ADDRESS: 27809 CONESTOGA DRIVE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES; APPLICANT: KYLE SMITH, WEST PALM GROUP;
  DESCRIPTION: A request for approval of a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination
  (NC-240123) for a new five-foot tall retaining wall and a Grading Permit (G-240122) for
  the export of 11.7 cubic yards of earth materials for a cut of a slope with a vertical height
  of more than three feet at its deepest point at the rear of the property.

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation for Planning Application No. PA-240121,
summarizing the staff report. She stated that the applicant is proposing to install a 5’ retaining
wall approximately 46’ in length along the west side property line. The retaining wall is set back
2’ from the property line; the retaining wall will also be set back 2’ from the driveway
encroachments of the neighboring property. The retaining wall is also 8’ from the ADU that exists
on the property.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, SEPTEMBER 3, 2024
  1
 Senior Planner Berry stated that the project meets the objectives of Neighborhood Compatibility
which are required and are outlined in the City’s Municipal Code. She stated that it has been
brought to staff’s attention that there are combination walls/fences along the site’s property line
that exceed the City’s maximum allowable height of 6’. Staff recommends that a condition of
approval is added to require that the walls/fences be reduced to a maximum of 6’ from the lowest
grade prior to issuance of a grading permit.

Senior Planner Berry stated that the grading permit criteria, as outlined in the City’s municipal
code, has also been met.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff received two public comments for this project, which were
attachments to the staff report. The first comment expressed concern with the project and its
proximity to the existing driveway. Staff met with this commenter who subsequently met with the
applicant who agreed to set back the retaining wall from the driveway. The second comment was
from the same commenter who expressed appreciation for the project revisions and ongoing
concerns with the size of the project area and desires to coordinate with the applicant regarding
the construction of the retaining wall.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommend that the Planning Commission approve PA-
240121, subject to the conditions outlined in the staff report and the additional condition that the
wall/fence along the side property line be reduced to a maximum 6’ in height from the lowest
finished grade prior to issuance of a grading permit.

VICE CHAIR OLSON inquired if the hillside is unstable or if there is any movement at the site.
Senior Planner Berry stated that there is no land movement; however, it is on a steep slope and
the fence is leaning forward towards the ADU.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked if the section of the wall/fence combination which
exceeds 6’ will be required to be rebuilt or if it will need to be modified to be in compliance with
the City’s height requirement. Senior Berry stated that staff will recommend reducing the height
of the fence which is on top of the retaining wall.

CHAIR MEDAWAR inquired if additional grading will be required to reduce the fence height.
Senior Planner Berry stated that no additional grading should be required.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked on whose property line is the driveway encroachment located.
Senior Planner Berry stated that the neighbor on the west side has a driveway which extends
onto the property line of the subject property.

Nicole Briggs, daughter of neighbor of applicant, stated that it is not her mother’s intention to be
against this project. She stated that she does not feel that the neighbor has been forthcoming with
the project beginning with the installation of the wall. She stated that her mother attempted to
speak with the neighbors but was informed that their attorneys were handling the issue. Ms. Briggs
attempted to contact their attorney who was unwilling to discuss any plans regarding the project.
Ms. Briggs expressed her concern with how close the retaining wall will be to the driveway and if
it could cause the driveway to sink in and if the wall will have enough support. Ms. Briggs stated
that it seems sections are being built separately and asked if the entire wall be built together. Ms.
Briggs provided pictures of the wall as it exists and stated that she would like a plan to make sure
that the driveway is protected and safe for her mother.

Nancy Briggs, neighbor of applicant, stated that she has lived in the City for fifty years. She stated
that there is bougainvillea up the driveway and sprinklers installed. She stated that when the
neighbor started building the wall began to lean; they did significant digging and there are
movement and cracks in her driveway. She stated that there is a need for a retaining wall but
does not believe that the additional planter is needed. Ms. Briggs explained her concern with the
grading. She thanked the commission for protecting the citizens of the City and stated that she
does not want more done that can destroy her property.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked if there is anything to suggest that the wall is not
properly placed due to the location of the driveway. Senior Planner stated that based on the
survey and submittals everything seems to be in order and the location on the plans is accurate.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that based on the plans it seems that the applicant
is not requesting anything other than what is existing and is tolerating the encroachment of the
neighboring driveway.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that the repair of fences are typically split between
the neighbors and likely needs to be updated.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, SEPTEMBER 3, 2024
  2
 CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that adding the retaining wall is stabilizing the hillside and is also to
the neighbor’s advantage.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked if the intention is to stabilize the slope. The applicant stated
that it is.

Nicole Briggs stated that the applicant is building a corner, and the wall is not being completed
and would like to make sure it is not going to cause more damage.

VICE CHAIR OLSON stated that this is a difficult retaining wall to build, and rely on the building
department, engineers, and geologists to do their jobs correctly which will result in a wall that
should stabilize the hillside. He asked if Ms. Briggs is asked that the wall be extended all the way
up the hillside. Ms. Briggs stated her concern is that she was informed that there will be another
section built in the future.

Kyle Smith, Architect, stated that he was not under the impression that there would be another
wall built in the future. Mr. Smith stated that the retaining wall was moved back due to the concerns
regarding the driveway. He stated that the original plan was to build a 70’ wall and there was
pushback from the neighbors, and it was reduced to approximately 48’. Mr. Smith stated that the
48’ wall is sufficient to retain the slope adjacent to the ADU.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN stated that the neighbor is trying to understand what is
being built now and in the future. She suggested that there be better communication between the
neighbors.

Gregory Andres, Owner, stated that he built and ADU and when he checked the survey they found
that the neighbors driveway encroaches 7’ inside the property line. She attempted to speak to the
neighbor to discuss the issue and she refused. Mr. Andres stated that he has done a soils report,
engineers, etc. who confirmed that there is degradation of the driveway or movement of the slope;
however, there is a potential which is the reason to install the retaining wall. Mr. Andres stated
that the fence is falling over due to the bougainvillea, and it is also a fire hazard and needs to be
addressed quickly. Mr. Andres also stated that the wall needs to be level with the foundation
adjacent to the ADU. He stated the driveway is large and there is a lot of room for a car to get
through. Mr. Andres stated that their attorneys are addressing the driveway encroachment.

CHAIR MEDAWAR asked if they are in litigation to acquire 7’ of his property and asked if the
driveway encroachment did not exist, would it extend the length of the property. Mr. Andres stated
yes.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that the applicant has complied and rely on the contractor
and surveyor to do the work property; if there is any damage to the driveway, the applicant will be
responsible for it.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS
to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240121, SUBJECT TO THE
  CONDITIONS OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT AND THE ADDITIONAL CONDITION
  THAT THE WALL/FENCE ALONG THE SIDE PROPERTY LINE BE REDUCED TO A
  MAXIMUM 6’ IN HEIGHT FROM THE LOWEST FINISHED GRADE PRIOR TO
  ISSUANCE OF A GRADING PERMIT.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN commented that the Planning Commission recognizes
when there is property right discussion it is sometimes beyond what the commission can be
responsible for. She recommended that the parties should try to communicate and resolve things
to lessen any issues.

AYES: MEDAWAR, OLSON, NICKLAS, REPP-LOADSMAN, SCHACHTER
NOES:
ABSENT: ROMANELLI, YOO
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application No.
PA-240121 approving a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination and Grading Permit for 27809
Conestoga drive. There is a 20-day appeal period by which any member of the public or the City
Council by their own motion may appeal this decision.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, SEPTEMBER 3, 2024
  3
 8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-230516; ADDRESS: 27525 NORRIS CENTER
  DRIVE, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES; APPLICANT: RYAN ASH ON BEHALF OF VESTAR;
  DESCRIPTION: Consideration of a Precise Plan of Design, a Commercial District Mixed-
  Use Development Permit, and a Development Agreement for a 90-unit apartment project
  on a 2-acre site in the Peninsula Shopping Center.

Senior Planner Berry stated that the applicant requested that this item be continued to the next
Planning Commission meeting on Monday, October 7, 2024. This item will be re-noticed as
required.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS
to,
  CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-230516 TO THE PLANNING
  COMMIISSION MEETING ON MONDAY, OCTOBER 7, 2024.

 Ayes: MEDAWAR, OLSON, NICKLAS, SCHACHTER, REPP-LOADSMAN
 Noes:
 Absent: ROMANELLI, YOO
 Abstain:

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER suggested that the applicants for PA-240121 work out a license
agreement that will need to be recorded.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about the retaining wall behind Bart Earle Way. Director
Naughton stated that staff is continuing to work with RPV staff to address this issue.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

NONE

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, AUGUST 13, 2024

B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, AUGUST 20, 2024 (SPECIAL MEETING)

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM 11A AND 11B

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR MEDAWAR adjourned the meeting at 7:48 p.m. to the next regular Planning Commission
meeting on Monday, October 7, 2024 at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos
Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Robert Medawar, Chair

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, SEPTEMBER 3, 2024
